name: Auriya Kaddu
subtitle: pumpkin in a sharp ground-mustard and yogurt gravy, the tangy course of a dham

ingredients.qty: 2 tbsp, soaked 2 hours and ground to a paste
ingredients.note: the auriya — this ground mustard is the whole dish
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free
balances the bite of the mustard

prepNotes: Soak the mustard seeds 2 hours, then grind with 2 tbsp of the soaking water to a fine grey paste. Ground dry, they stay gritty and turn bitter.
Take the yogurt out of the fridge an hour ahead. Cold yogurt splits the moment it meets a hot pan.
Whisk the yogurt with the turmeric and chilli powder before it goes anywhere near the heat.

steps.text: Heat the ghee and mustard oil together until the mustard oil stops smelling raw, about 1 minute.
Crackle the fenugreek seeds and broken red chillies for 20 seconds, then add the hing.
steps.tip: Fenugreek goes from fragrant to bitter in about 10 seconds. Pull it the moment it turns reddish-brown.

steps.text: Add the pumpkin cubes and toss over medium heat 5 minutes until the edges catch a little colour.
Take the pan off the heat for a minute so it cools, then pour in the whisked spiced yogurt and stir continuously.
steps.tip: Off the heat and stirring — this is the only reliable way to stop the yogurt curdling.

steps.text: Return to a low flame and cook, stirring in one direction, until the yogurt loses its raw smell and thickens slightly, about 4 minutes.
Stir in the ground mustard paste, 200ml water and salt. Simmer uncovered 12 minutes until the pumpkin is tender at a knifepoint but not falling apart.
steps.tip: Never boil the mustard hard — heat turns it acrid. A bare simmer only.

steps.text: Add the amchur and sugar, cook 2 minutes more and taste. It should be sour, mustardy and only faintly sweet.
Rest 5 minutes off the heat and serve with rice as part of a dham.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat over the lowest flame with a spoon of water — a hard reheat splits the yogurt and sharpens the mustard.
